title: Let Us, with a Gladsome Mind
description: Let Us, with a Gladsome Mind in Tonic Solfa to MONKLAND: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the eight verses and the refrain, and a piano.
about: John Milton wrote these words, a paraphrase of Psalm 136, in 1623, when he was fifteen; they were first printed in his Poems of 1645. The tune MONKLAND comes from a melody by John Antes, arranged by John Bernard Wilkes for Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861).
underlay: Let us, with a glad_-some_ mind, Praise the Lord, for He is kind. For His_ mer-cies aye en-dure, Ev-er_ faith-ful, ev-er sure.

lines: Let us, with a gladsome mind,
Praise the Lord, for He is kind.
Let us blaze His name abroad,
For of gods He is the God.
Filled the new made world with light.
He hath, with a piteous eye,
Caused all day his course to run.
Th’hornèd moon to shine by night;
All things living He doth feed,
His full hand supplies their need.
Let us, with a gladsome mind,
Praise the Lord, for He is kind.
